definitions.explanation: the first year of something such as an era, a policy, a system, or a person's time in a position

examples.japanese: {初年|しょねん}の{売上|うりあげ}は{好調|こうちょう}だった。
examples.english: Sales in the first year were strong.

examples.japanese: {制度|せいど}{導入|どうにゅう}{初年|しょねん}は{混乱|こんらん}が{多|おお}かった。
examples.english: There was a lot of confusion in the first year of the system's introduction.

examples.japanese: この{大学|だいがく}では{初年|しょねん}に{基礎科目|きそかもく}を{中心|ちゅうしん}に{学|まな}び、{二年目|にねんめ}から{専門|せんもん}に{入|はい}る。
examples.english: At this university, students focus on foundational subjects in the first year and enter their specialty from the second year.

notes:
A formal term for the first year of a period, often used in business, academic, and governmental contexts. Frequently appears in compound forms and is common in news and official reports.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {初年度|しょねんど}: first fiscal year (the most common compound form)
- {初年|しょねん}{効果|こうか}: first-year effect
- {導入|どうにゅう}{初年|しょねん}: first year of introduction
- {開業|かいぎょう}{初年|しょねん}: first year of business

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {一年目|いちねんめ}: first year — the general, everyday way to say "first year"
- {元年|がんねん}: first year of an era — specifically the first year of a Japanese imperial era or a symbolic new beginning
- {初年度|しょねんど}: first fiscal year — the compound form, most commonly used in business and government
